tasks.title: Hydraulics > Flow Calculator (Q = K√P solver)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/flow-calculator.test.ts
tasks.spec:
Implement the AutoSprink 'Flow Calculator' (Hydraulics menu): given any TWO of {flow Q (gpm), K-factor (gpm/psi^0.5), pressure P (psi)}, derive the third using the cited sprinkler discharge formula Q = K * sqrt(P).

Exports (exact):
- export interface FlowCalcInput { flowGpm?: number; kFactor?: number; pressurePsi?: number; }
- export interface FlowCalcResult { flowGpm: number; kFactor: number; pressurePsi: number; solvedFor: 'flowGpm' | 'kFactor' | 'pressurePsi'; formula: 'Q = K * sqrt(P)'; }
- export function solveFlow(input: FlowCalcInput): FlowCalcResult — throws an Error with a clear message when fewer or more than exactly 2 fields are given, when any given value is not a finite positive number, or when pressure must be derived from K=0.

Math: flow = K*sqrt(P); K = Q/sqrt(P); P = (Q/K)^2.
Tests must cover: solve each of the 3 unknowns with K=5.6, P=25 -> Q=28 exactly; round-trip consistency; each error case (0 fields, 1 field, 3 fields, negative/zero/NaN values).

tasks.title: Hydraulics > Show Pipe Volumes
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/pipe-volume.test.ts
tasks.spec:
Implement the AutoSprink 'Show Pipe Volumes' calculation: water volume of pipe segments from internal diameter and length.

Use EXACTLY these internal diameters (inches), from ANSI/ASME B36.10M steel pipe tables (verify against adopted edition before regulated use):
SCH40: 0.5->0.622, 0.75->0.824, 1->1.049, 1.25->1.380, 1.5->1.610, 2->2.067, 2.5->2.469, 3->3.068, 4->4.026, 6->6.065, 8->7.981
SCH10: 1->1.097, 1.25->1.442, 1.5->1.682, 2->2.157, 2.5->2.635, 3->3.260, 4->4.260, 6->6.357, 8->8.329
Gallons per cubic foot: 7.48052.

Exports (exact):
- export function internalDiameterIn(material: 'STEEL_SCH40' | 'STEEL_SCH10' | 'CPVC' | 'COPPER', nominalIn: number): number — SCH40 table for STEEL_SCH40 and (as a documented approximation) CPVC/COPPER; SCH10 table for STEEL_SCH10; throws on unknown nominal size.
- export interface SegmentVolume { segmentId: string; gallons: number; cubicFeet: number; }
- export interface VolumeReport { perSegment: SegmentVolume[]; totalGallons: number; totalCubicFeet: number; }
- export function pipeVolumes(segments: Array<{ id: string; diameterIn: number; lengthFt: number; material: 'STEEL_SCH40' | 'STEEL_SCH10' | 'CPVC' | 'COPPER' }>): VolumeReport

Math per segment: radiusFt = internalDiameterIn/24; cubicFeet = PI * radiusFt^2 * lengthFt; gallons = cubicFeet * 7.48052. Totals are sums. Skip (omit from perSegment) segments with non-positive length, but throw on unknown nominal sizes.
Tests: 2in SCH40 x 100ft -> cubicFeet = PI*(2.067/24)^2*100 (assert with toBeCloseTo, 4 digits) and gallons = that * 7.48052; SCH10 vs SCH40 differ for same nominal; totals sum; zero-length skipped; unknown nominal throws.

tasks.title: Commands > Break / Divide / Reverse (pure segment ops)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/segment-ops.test.ts
tasks.spec:
Implement pure versions of three AutoSprink Commands-menu operations over the network model (see model.ts for Node/Segment shapes; Node.pos is {x,y,z} feet; Segment has from/to node ids, diameterIn, lengthFt, role, material).

Exports (exact):
- export interface NetworkSlice { nodes: Array<{ id: string; type: string; pos: { x: number; y: number; z: number } }>; segments: Array<{ id: string; from: string; to: string; diameterIn: number; lengthFt: number; role: string; material: string }>; }
- export function breakSegment(net: NetworkSlice, segmentId: string, t: number, newNodeId: string, seg1Id: string, seg2Id: string): NetworkSlice — split one segment at parameter t (0<t<1, throw otherwise or when ids collide/missing): insert a new node of type 'FITTING' linearly interpolated between the endpoints' positions, replace the segment with two segments (from->new with lengthFt*t, new->to with lengthFt*(1-t)), preserving diameterIn/role/material. Pure: returns a NEW object, inputs untouched.
- export function divideSegment(net: NetworkSlice, segmentId: string, parts: number, idPrefix: string): NetworkSlice — divide into N equal parts (integer 2..50, throw otherwise) by repeated interpolation: creates N-1 nodes `${idPrefix}_n1..` and N segments `${idPrefix}_s1..`, equal lengths summing to the original lengthFt (each lengthFt/N). Pure.
- export function reverseSegment(net: NetworkSlice, segmentId: string): NetworkSlice — swap from/to of one segment. Pure. Throws when the segment id is missing.

Tests: break at t=0.25 puts the new node at the 25% interpolated position and lengths 25/75 of original; divide a 30ft segment into 3 -> 3 segments of 10ft each, 2 new nodes, connectivity chain intact (from/to ids form a path from original endpoints); reverse swaps endpoints and double-reverse restores; purity (original object unchanged, use structuredClone comparison); all throw cases.

tasks.title: Tools > Line/Polyline/Arc/Circle/Rectangle/Point (element model)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/drawing-elements.test.ts
tasks.spec:
Implement the pure data model for six AutoSprink Tools-menu drawing primitives (2D plan-space, units = feet): Line Segment, Polyline, Arc, Circle, Rectangle, Point.

Exports (exact):
- export interface Pt { x: number; y: number; }
- export type DrawingElement = { id: string } & ( { kind: 'line'; a: Pt; b: Pt } | { kind: 'polyline'; points: Pt[] } | { kind: 'arc'; center: Pt; radiusFt: number; startDeg: number; endDeg: number } | { kind: 'circle'; center: Pt; radiusFt: number } | { kind: 'rectangle'; corner: Pt; widthFt: number; heightFt: number } | { kind: 'point'; at: Pt } );
- Constructors, each validating finiteness and throwing on invalid input: makeLine(id, a, b) (a!=b), makePolyline(id, points) (>=2 points), makeArc(id, center, radiusFt>0, startDeg, endDeg) (angles finite, normalized into [0,360)), makeCircle(id, center, radiusFt>0), makeRectangle(id, corner, widthFt>0, heightFt>0), makePoint(id, at).
- export function elementLengthFt(el: DrawingElement): number — line: Euclidean distance; polyline: sum of consecutive distances; arc: 2*PI*r*(sweep/360) where sweep = (endDeg-startDeg+360)%360 (full circle when sweep computes to 0 AND start!==end is impossible after normalization, so sweep 0 means 0); circle: circumference 2*PI*r; rectangle: perimeter 2*(w+h); point: 0.
- export function elementAreaFt2(el: DrawingElement): number — circle: PI*r^2; rectangle: w*h; closed polyline (first point equals last point): shoelace formula absolute value; all others: 0.

Tests: 3-4-5 line length 5; polyline lengths sum; quarter arc (r=10, 0..90) length = 2*PI*10*0.25; circle area PI*r^2; rectangle perimeter and area; closed square polyline (0,0)(10,0)(10,10)(0,10)(0,0) area 100 via shoelace; open polyline area 0; every constructor throw case (NaN coords, radius<=0, <2 polyline points, degenerate line, non-positive rectangle dims).

tasks.title: Commands > Tag Leaks (open pipe ends)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/leak-check.test.ts
tasks.spec:
Implement the AutoSprink 'Tag Leaks' analysis: find OPEN PIPE ENDS in the sprinkler network — connection points where water would escape. A leak is (a) a segment endpoint referencing a node id that does not exist (dangling reference), or (b) a node of degree 1 (exactly one attached segment) whose type is NOT one of the closed/terminal types: 'HEAD', 'SOURCE', 'VALVE'.

Exports (exact):
- export interface Leak { nodeId: string; reason: 'dangling-reference' | 'open-end'; segmentIds: string[]; }
- export interface LeakReport { leaks: Leak[]; checkedNodes: number; checkedSegments: number; clean: boolean; }
- export function findLeaks(net: { nodes: Array<{ id: string; type: string }>; segments: Array<{ id: string; from: string; to: string }> }): LeakReport

Rules: degree = number of segment endpoints touching the node (a self-loop counts 2). For dangling references the Leak.nodeId is the MISSING id and segmentIds lists the referencing segments. Sort leaks by nodeId for determinism. clean = leaks.length === 0. Pure function, inputs untouched.

Tests: linear run HEAD - FITTING - FITTING - SOURCE is clean; chop the last segment -> the now degree-1 FITTING is an open-end leak; a segment pointing at a nonexistent id is a dangling-reference leak listing that segment; isolated degree-0 fitting node is NOT a leak (it is unpiped, not open); HEAD/SOURCE/VALVE at degree 1 are never leaks; determinism (sorted by nodeId).

tasks.title: Hydraulics > Density/area per-head demand floor
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/density-demand.test.ts
tasks.spec: Implement the NFPA-13 density/area per-head demand floor as a pure module. Use EXACTLY these design densities (gpm/ft^2), the low-point of the NFPA-13 density/area curves, edition-dependent — every export carries a citation string ending "Verify adopted edition.": LIGHT→0.10, ORDINARY_1→0.15, ORDINARY_2→0.20, EXTRA_1→0.30, EXTRA_2→0.40. Use EXACTLY these per-head max protection areas (ft^2), matching the repo's cited MAX_PROTECTION_AREA_SQFT: LIGHT→225, ORDINARY_1→130, ORDINARY_2→130, EXTRA_1→100, EXTRA_2→100. Use EXACTLY these minimum remote design areas (ft^2): LIGHT→1500, ORDINARY_1→1500, ORDINARY_2→1500, EXTRA_1→2500, EXTRA_2→2500. Exports (exact): `export type HazardClass = 'LIGHT' | 'ORDINARY_1' | 'ORDINARY_2' | 'EXTRA_1' | 'EXTRA_2';` `export interface CitedNumber { value: number; citation: string; }` `export const DESIGN_DENSITY_GPM_SQFT: Record<HazardClass, CitedNumber>;` `export const PER_HEAD_AREA_SQFT: Record<HazardClass, CitedNumber>;` `export const MIN_REMOTE_AREA_SQFT: Record<HazardClass, CitedNumber>;` `export function densityFloorGpm(hazard: HazardClass, perHeadAreaSqFt?: number): number` — density × (perHeadAreaSqFt ?? PER_HEAD_AREA_SQFT[hazard].value); throws on non-finite/non-positive override. `export function pressureForFlow(flowGpm: number, kFactor: number): number` — (Q/K)^2; throws on K<=0 or Q<0. `export interface HeadDemand { flowGpm: number; pressurePsi: number; governedBy: 'min-pressure' | 'density-floor'; citation: string; }` `export function effectiveHeadDemand(kFactor: number, minOperatingPsi: number, hazard: HazardClass, perHeadAreaSqFt?: number): HeadDemand` — qMin = kFactor*sqrt(minOperatingPsi); qFloor = densityFloorGpm(...); if qFloor > qMin return {flowGpm: qFloor, pressurePsi: pressureForFlow(qFloor, kFactor), governedBy: 'density-floor', citation: DESIGN_DENSITY_GPM_SQFT[hazard].citation} else {flowGpm: qMin, pressurePsi: minOperatingPsi, governedBy: 'min-pressure', citation: <minimum-operating-pressure citation string authored in this module>}; throws on kFactor<=0 or minOperatingPsi<=0. Tests: ORDINARY_1, K=5.6, 7 psi → qMin=5.6*sqrt(7)≈14.8167, qFloor=0.15*130=19.5 → density-floor governs, pressurePsi=(19.5/5.6)^2≈12.1249 (toBeCloseTo 3 digits); LIGHT, K=5.6, 7 psi → qFloor=0.10*225=22.5 > 14.8167 → density-floor; LIGHT, K=8.0, 16 psi → qMin=32 > 22.5 → min-pressure governs with pressurePsi=16; perHeadAreaSqFt override changes the floor linearly; every throw case; every CitedNumber.citation is a non-empty string containing "Verify adopted edition".

tasks.title: View > Pan/zoom viewport transform math (pure)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/viewport.test.ts
tasks.spec: Pure 2D viewport math for a plan canvas: stagePt = planPt*scale + offset. Exports (exact): `export interface Viewport { scale: number; offsetX: number; offsetY: number; }` `export interface Pt { x: number; y: number; }` `export interface Bounds { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number; }` `export const MIN_SCALE = 1e-6;` `export const MAX_SCALE = 1e6;` `export const ZOOM_STEP = 1.1;` `export function fitViewport(bounds: Bounds, stageW: number, stageH: number, paddingPx: number): Viewport` — uniform scale = min((stageW-2*paddingPx)/boundsW, (stageH-2*paddingPx)/boundsH) clamped to [MIN_SCALE, MAX_SCALE], offsets center the bounds in the stage; for zero/negative bounds dimensions or stage dims <= 2*paddingPx return {scale: 1, offsetX: stageW/2, offsetY: stageH/2}. `export function toStagePt(vp: Viewport, plan: Pt): Pt` — {x: plan.x*vp.scale+vp.offsetX, y: plan.y*vp.scale+vp.offsetY}. `export function toPlanPt(vp: Viewport, stage: Pt): Pt` — exact inverse. `export function zoomAt(vp: Viewport, stageCursor: Pt, factor: number): Viewport` — newScale = clamp(vp.scale*factor, MIN_SCALE, MAX_SCALE); the plan point under stageCursor must map to the SAME stage point after zoom: newOffset = stageCursor - planPtUnderCursor*newScale; throws on non-finite or non-positive factor. `export function panBy(vp: Viewport, dxPx: number, dyPx: number): Viewport` — offsets += deltas; throws on non-finite deltas. `export function zoomPercent(vp: Viewport, fitScale: number): number` — round(100*vp.scale/fitScale); throws when fitScale <= 0. All functions pure (return new objects). Tests: toPlanPt(toStagePt(p)) round-trips (toBeCloseTo 10 digits); fitViewport of bounds {0,0,100,50} into 1000x600 stage with padding 20 gives scale = min(960/100, 560/50) = 9.6 and centers; zoomAt invariant: for vp {scale:2, offsetX:10, offsetY:-5}, cursor {x:300,y:200}, factor 1.5 — toPlanPt before === toPlanPt after at the cursor (toBeCloseTo); repeated zoomAt clamps at MAX_SCALE; panBy(3,-4) shifts a mapped point by exactly (3,-4) stage px; degenerate-bounds fallback; throw cases.

tasks.title: Edit > Multi-selection set + window/crossing marquee hit tests (pure)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/selection-set.test.ts
tasks.spec: Pure multi-selection model and marquee geometry. Exports (exact): `export interface Pt { x: number; y: number; }` `export interface Rect { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number; }` `export type SelKind = 'node' | 'segment' | 'room';` `export interface SelectionSet { nodeIds: string[]; segmentIds: string[]; roomIds: string[]; }` `export function emptySelection(): SelectionSet` — all arrays empty. `export function selectionCount(sel: SelectionSet): number` — sum of lengths. `export function togglePick(sel: SelectionSet, kind: SelKind, id: string, additive: boolean): SelectionSet` — pure; non-additive returns a selection containing ONLY that id in its kind list; additive toggles membership (add if absent, remove if present) keeping other kinds; output arrays sorted lexicographically; throws on empty id. `export function normalizeRect(a: Pt, b: Pt): Rect` — min/max of the two corners. `export function pointInRect(p: Pt, r: Rect): boolean` — inclusive bounds. `export function segmentInRect(a: Pt, b: Pt, r: Rect): boolean` — both endpoints pointInRect. `export function segmentIntersectsRect(a: Pt, b: Pt, r: Rect): boolean` — true when either endpoint is inside OR the segment properly crosses any of the 4 rect edges; implement a `segmentsIntersect(p1,p2,p3,p4)` helper via orientation sign tests: orient(p,q,r) = sign((q.x-p.x)*(r.y-p.y)-(q.y-p.y)*(r.x-p.x)); segments intersect when orientations of (p1,p2,p3)/(p1,p2,p4) differ AND (p3,p4,p1)/(p3,p4,p2) differ; treat collinear-overlap (any orient 0 with the point's coordinates within the other segment's bounding box, inclusive) as intersecting. `export interface MarqueeItems { nodes: Array<{ id: string; at: Pt }>; segments: Array<{ id: string; a: Pt; b: Pt }>; }` `export function marqueeSelect(items: MarqueeItems, cornerA: Pt, cornerB: Pt, mode: 'window' | 'crossing'): SelectionSet` — window: nodes with pointInRect, segments with segmentInRect (fully contained); crossing: nodes with pointInRect, segments with segmentIntersectsRect; roomIds always []; outputs sorted; pure. Tests: togglePick non-additive replaces across kinds; additive add/remove round-trip; sorted determinism; rect normalization from any corner pair; segment fully inside selected in both modes; segment crossing one rect edge selected ONLY in crossing mode; segment fully outside never selected; collinear segment lying along a rect edge counts as crossing; marquee over mixed items returns exactly the expected sorted ids; throw on empty id.

tasks.title: Import > 1881 kernel DXF entities → SprinklerNetwork slice (pure)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/kernel-import.test.ts
tasks.spec: Pure builder turning already-parsed kernel-DXF entities into network nodes/segments. The 1881 kernel (`design.dxf`) carries heads as CIRCLE entities on layer `HALOFIRE_HEADS` and pipes as LINE entities on layer `HALOFIRE_PIPES` (verified: 1303 head circles, 1758 pipe lines). This module does NOT parse DXF text — it consumes plain entity inputs so tests are synthetic. Exports (exact): `export const KERNEL_HEAD_LAYER = 'HALOFIRE_HEADS';` `export const KERNEL_PIPE_LAYER = 'HALOFIRE_PIPES';` `export const SNAP_TOLERANCE_FT = 0.05;` `export interface KernelCircle { cx: number; cy: number; layer: string; }` `export interface KernelLine { x1: number; y1: number; x2: number; y2: number; layer: string; }` `export interface KernelImportOpts { ftPerUnit: number; headLayer?: string; pipeLayer?: string; zFt?: number; defaultDiameterIn?: number; }` `export interface KernelNetwork { nodes: Array<{ id: string; type: 'HEAD' | 'TEE' | 'ELBOW'; pos: { x: number; y: number; z: number } }>; segments: Array<{ id: string; from: string; to: string; diameterIn: number; lengthFt: number; role: 'BRANCH'; material: 'STEEL_SCH40' }>; headCount: number; junctionCount: number; droppedZeroLength: number; }` `export function buildKernelNetwork(circles: KernelCircle[], lines: KernelLine[], opts: KernelImportOpts): KernelNetwork`. Algorithm (exact): (1) throw on non-finite/non-positive ftPerUnit; let head layer = opts.headLayer ?? KERNEL_HEAD_LAYER, pipe layer = opts.pipeLayer ?? KERNEL_PIPE_LAYER, z = opts.zFt ?? 0, dia = opts.defaultDiameterIn ?? 1. (2) Scale every coordinate by ftPerUnit. (3) For each circle on the head layer create a HEAD node id `head_<index1Based>` at (cx, cy) scaled, pos {x, y: z, z: cy→use pos {x: scaledCx, y: zFt, z: scaledCy}} — plan x→pos.x, plan y→pos.z, elevation→pos.y (matches model.ts 'y is up'). (4) For each line endpoint on the pipe layer, snap to an existing node when the 2D plan distance (x/z plane) <= SNAP_TOLERANCE_FT, preferring HEAD nodes, else the earliest-created junction; otherwise create a junction node id `jct_<n>` (n increments from 1) at that point. (5) After all segments exist, set each junction node's type: 'TEE' when its degree (number of segment endpoints touching it) >= 3, else 'ELBOW'. (6) Each pipe line becomes segment id `pipe_<index1Based>` with from/to = resolved node ids, lengthFt = 2D Euclidean distance (in feet) rounded to 4 decimals, role 'BRANCH', material 'STEEL_SCH40', diameterIn = dia; lines whose scaled length <= SNAP_TOLERANCE_FT are dropped and counted in droppedZeroLength. (7) Ignore circles/lines on other layers entirely. headCount/junctionCount are the created counts. Pure: inputs untouched; deterministic ids by input order. Tests: one circle + one line ending within tolerance of it → segment.from or .to is `head_1` (no duplicate junction); H-shape of 3 lines meeting at a shared point → that junction degree 3 → 'TEE', the others 'ELBOW' or HEAD per setup; ftPerUnit 0.25 scales a 40-unit line to lengthFt 10; zero-length line dropped and counted; off-layer entities ignored; custom layer names honored; mapping check pos {x, y: zFt, z: planY}; determinism (same input twice → deep-equal output); throw on ftPerUnit <= 0.

tasks.title: Reports > Hydraulic calc summary text formatter (pure)

tasks.spec:
Pure plain-text formatter for a hydraulic result — the submittal-lane "calc summary". It consumes a structural input (NOT importing solver internals) so it stays decoupled. Exports (exact): `export interface ReportNodeRow { id: string; pressurePsi: number; flowGpm: number; }` `export interface ReportSegmentRow { id: string; flowGpm: number; frictionPsi: number; velocityFps: number; }` `export interface ReportInput { projectName: string; hazard: string; demandGpm: number; demandPsiAtRiser: number; supply?: { staticPsi: number; residualPsi: number; flowGpm: number; availablePsiAtDemand: number; adequate: boolean }; nodes: ReportNodeRow[]; segments: ReportSegmentRow[]; disclaimer: string; citations: string[]; }` `export const REPORT_HEADER = 'HALOFIRE CAD - HYDRAULIC DESIGN AID SUMMARY';` `export function formatNumber(n: number, decimals: number): string` — toFixed(decimals); throws on non-finite n or negative/non-integer decimals. `export function formatHydraulicReport(input: ReportInput): string`. Layout (exact): line 1 REPORT_HEADER; line 2 `Project: <projectName>`; line 3 `Hazard: <hazard>`; line 4 blank; line 5 `SYSTEM DEMAND: <demandGpm,1>gpm @ <demandPsiAtRiser,1> psi at riser` (numbers via formatNumber with 1 decimal, format exactly `DEMAND: X.X gpm @ Y.Y psi at riser` prefixed `SYSTEM `); then when supply is present: `SUPPLY: static <staticPsi,1> psi, residual <residualPsi,1> psi @ <flowGpm,1> gpm` and `AVAILABLE @ DEMAND: <availablePsiAtDemand,1> psi -> <ADEQUATE|INADEQUATE>`; when supply is absent the single line `SUPPLY: none provided (demand-only result)`; blank line; `NODES (<count>)` followed by one line per node `  <id padded right to 16 chars with spaces>  P=<pressurePsi,2> psi  Q=<flowGpm,2> gpm`; blank line; `SEGMENTS (<count>)` followed by one line per segment `  <id padded right to 16 chars>  Q=<flowGpm,2> gpm  dP=<frictionPsi,3> psi  v=<velocityFps,2> ft/s`; blank line; `CITATIONS:` then `  - <each citation>` in input order; blank line; the disclaimer verbatim as the final line(s). Rows are emitted in INPUT ORDER (caller sorts). Pad ids longer than 16 chars without truncation (pad-to-at-least-16). Throws when disclaimer is an empty string or citations is empty (fail-closed honesty: a report without citations/disclaimer must not be producible). Tests: golden full report string for a 2-node/1-segment input with supply (assert exact string equality, template literal in test); demand-only variant contains 'SUPPLY: none provided'; INADEQUATE rendered when adequate=false; long id padding; throw on empty disclaimer; throw on empty citations; formatNumber rounding (1.005 with 2 decimals via toFixed semantics — assert toFixed output equality, not an invented rounding rule).

tasks.title: Auto Draw > Auto Size (schedule pipe sizing)
tasks.gate: cd apps/cad && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run test/pipe-sizing.test.ts
tasks.spec: Pure pipe schedule sizing: pick the smallest nominal size whose velocity stays within a limit for a given flow.
